title: 5 Signs Your Dog Needs a New Collar
author: Paw & Found
excerpt: Is your dog's collar past its prime? Here are five tell-tale signs it's time for an upgrade — plus what to look for in a replacement.
contentHtml:
5 Signs Your Dog Needs a New Collar

Your dog's collar is one of the most important accessories they'll ever wear. It holds their ID tags, keeps them safe on walks, and says a lot about their personality. But how do you know when it's time for a replacement?

Here are five signs to watch for:

1. Fraying or Worn Edges

If you notice threads coming loose, the edges looking rough, or the material thinning out, it's time. A frayed collar can snap unexpectedly — and that's the last thing you want during a walk.

2. It's Hard to Buckle

A collar that's difficult to fasten or unfasten is a safety hazard. Buckles should click smoothly every time. If yours is sticking, rusting, or stiff, replace it before it fails completely.

3. Fading or Discoloration

Sun, sweat, and the elements take a toll on collar materials. While a little fading is cosmetic, significant discoloration can indicate the material is breaking down structurally.

4. Your Dog Has Outgrown It

Puppies grow fast, and even adult dogs can gain or lose weight. A good rule of thumb: you should be able to fit two fingers comfortably between the collar and your dog's neck. If it's too tight or too loose, get a new one.

5. Smells That Won't Go Away

Some collars absorb odours over time, especially if they get wet frequently. If washing doesn't help, it's time for a fresh start.

What to Look For in a New Collar

When shopping for a replacement, choose one that's:

  • Durable — genuine leather or heavy-duty nylon lasts longer
  • Comfortable — padded options reduce chafing
  • Reflective — for visibility during evening walks
  • The right size — measure your dog's neck before buying

title: How to Keep Your Cat Happy with Minimal Effort
author: Paw & Found
excerpt: Cats are low-maintenance, but they still need the right setup to thrive. Here's how to create a happy home for your feline friend without a ton of work.
contentHtml:
How to Keep Your Cat Happy with Minimal Effort

Cats have a reputation for being independent — and it's well-earned. But even the most self-sufficient feline needs a few key things to be truly happy. The good news? Once you set these up, they practically run themselves.

1. Get the Litter Situation Right

Bad litter = unhappy cat = messes outside the box. It's that simple.

  • Use quality litter that clumps well and controls odour
  • Scoop daily (takes 2 minutes)
  • Deep clean the box every 2-3 weeks
  • One box per cat + one extra is the golden rule

👉 Shop our cat litter — premium clumping litter that keeps smells under control

2. Provide Scratching Surfaces

Cats need to scratch — it's instinctual. If you don't provide appropriate surfaces, your furniture becomes the scratching post. A simple cardboard scratcher or sisal mat is usually enough.

3. Keep Them Entertained

A bored cat is a destructive cat. But you don't need to entertain them 24/7. Just:

  • Leave a few toys out and rotate them weekly
  • Place a bird feeder near a window (free cat TV!)
  • Set up a cardboard box or two (seriously, they love them)

👉 Squeaky ball | Plush fox toy

4. Fresh Water, Always

Cats are notoriously bad at staying hydrated. A simple fountain (moving water encourages drinking) can make a huge difference to their health.

5. Regular Grooming (Even for Short Hair)

Brushing your cat once or twice a week reduces hairballs, keeps their coat healthy, and is a great bonding activity. Plus, less fur on your furniture.

👉 Gentle grooming brush

The Secret to a Happy Cat

It's not about having the most expensive toys or the biggest cat tree. It's about consistency: clean litter, fresh water, regular meals, and a little bit of your time every day. Do those things, and your cat will be perfectly content.

title: The Ultimate Puppy Starter Kit: What You Really Need

excerpt: Bringing home a new puppy? Skip the overwhelm. Here's exactly what you need to have ready — from feeding supplies to grooming essentials.
contentHtml:
The Ultimate Puppy Starter Kit: What You Really Need

Bringing home a new puppy is one of the most exciting days — but it's easy to get overwhelmed by the endless checklist of things to buy. We've narrowed it down to the essentials so you can focus on what really matters: bonding with your new best friend.

1. Food & Water Bowls

Start with sturdy, non-slip bowls that won't slide across the floor during mealtime. Ceramic or stainless steel are best — they're easy to clean and don't harbour bacteria.

2. A Comfortable Bed

Your puppy will sleep a lot — up to 18-20 hours a day! A cozy, washable bed gives them a safe spot to rest. Look for one with raised edges that makes them feel secure.

👉 Browse pet beds

3. Collar, Leash & ID Tag

Even if your puppy stays indoors most of the time, accidents happen. A well-fitted collar with an ID tag is essential from day one. Choose an adjustable collar that can grow with them.

4. Grooming Supplies

Get your puppy used to being brushed early — it makes grooming much easier as they grow. A good brush removes loose fur, distributes natural oils, and is a great bonding activity.

👉 Gentle grooming brush

5. Toys, Toys, Toys

Puppies explore the world with their mouths. Providing plenty of appropriate toys saves your shoes, furniture, and sanity. Rotate toys to keep things interesting.

👉 Squeaky ball | Plush fox toy

6. Gentle Shampoo

Puppies get messy. A mild, puppy-safe shampoo is a must for bath time. Look for something pH-balanced and free of harsh chemicals.

You don't need everything in the pet store on day one. Start with these essentials, and add as you go. Your puppy will love you for the attention and care — not the stuff.

title: The Ultimate Guide to Pet Apparel Sizing
author: Paw & Found Team
excerpt: Getting the right fit for your pet's clothing can be tricky. Our comprehensive sizing guide helps you measure and choose the perfect apparel.
contentHtml:
The Ultimate Guide to Pet Apparel Sizing

Finding the perfect fit for your pet's wardrobe doesn't have to be a guessing game. Follow this guide to ensure your pup looks stylish and feels comfortable.

How to Measure Your Pet

You'll need a soft measuring tape. Measure your pet while they're standing on all fours.

1. Neck Circumference

Measure around the base of the neck, where a collar would sit. Add one finger's width for comfort.

2. Chest Girth

Measure the widest part of the chest, just behind the front legs. This is the most important measurement for most apparel.

3. Back Length

Measure from the base of the neck (between the shoulder blades) to the base of the tail. This determines the length of shirts and hoodies.

Sizing by Breed

| Breed Type | Back Length | Chest Girth | Recommended Size |

|------------|-------------|-------------|------------------|

| Chihuahua / Yorkie | 8-10" | 10-14" | XS |

| French Bulldog / Pug | 10-12" | 14-18" | S |

| Beagle / Corgi | 12-16" | 18-24" | M |

| Border Collie / Husky | 16-20" | 24-30" | L |

| Labrador / Golden Retriever | 20-24" | 30-36" | XL |

Our Apparel Collection

We offer a range of sizes from XS to XL in all our apparel:

  • Good Dog Club T-Shirt — Classic cotton tee, perfect for everyday wear
  • Adventure Pup Graphic Tee — Organic cotton with a fun design
  • Cozy Hoodie Pullover — Fleece-lined warmth for chilly walks

Pro Tips

  • When in doubt, size up. A slightly loose fit is better than too tight.
  • Check the fabric. Stretchy materials like cotton blends are more forgiving.
  • Watch for restrictions. Make sure your pet can move, eat, and potty comfortably.

title: 5 Tips for a Happy, Healthy Pet
author: Paw & Found Team
excerpt: From proper nutrition to regular exercise, discover our top tips for keeping your furry friend happy and healthy.
contentHtml:
5 Tips for a Happy, Healthy Pet

As pet parents, we all want the best for our furry companions. Here are five essential tips to keep your pet thriving.

1. Proper Nutrition Matters

A balanced diet is the foundation of good health. Choose high-quality pet food that's appropriate for your pet's age, size, and activity level. Our Essentials category has a great selection of nutritious food options.

2. Regular Exercise

Daily exercise is crucial for both physical and mental health. Dogs need walks, runs, and playtime, while cats benefit from interactive toys and climbing structures. Check out our Accessories for fun toys and leashes.

3. Routine Vet Checkups

Preventive care is key. Regular vet visits can catch health issues early. Keep up with vaccinations, dental care, and parasite prevention.

4. Grooming and Hygiene

Regular grooming keeps your pet's coat healthy and reduces shedding. Our Supplies section has shampoos, brushes, and grooming tools to make bath time a breeze.

5. Mental Stimulation

Bored pets can develop behavioral issues. Puzzle toys, training sessions, and new experiences keep their minds sharp. Try our Plush Squeaky Fox Toy for hours of interactive fun!

title: How to Choose the Right Cat Litter
author: Paw & Found Team
excerpt: Not all cat litters are created equal. Learn the differences between clumping, crystal, and natural litters to find the perfect match for your cat.
contentHtml:
How to Choose the Right Cat Litter

With so many options on the market, choosing the right cat litter can feel overwhelming. Here's everything you need to know.

Types of Cat Litter

Clumping Clay Litter

The most popular choice. Forms solid clumps when wet, making scooping easy.

Pros: Excellent odor control, easy to clean, cost-effective

Cons: Can be dusty, heavier to carry

Our Premium Clumping Cat Litter (40lb) is 99.9% dust-free with odor-locking technology — a top choice for odor-sensitive homes.

Crystal (Silica Gel) Litter

Made from silica gel crystals that absorb moisture and dry out solid waste.

Pros: Very lightweight, excellent odor control, less frequent changes needed

Cons: More expensive, some cats don't like the texture

Natural/Biodegradable Litter

Made from materials like pine, wheat, corn, or paper.

Pros: Eco-friendly, flushable options available, generally low dust

Cons: May not clump as well, can track more

Choosing by Your Cat's Preferences

  • Senior cats or kittens — Look for low-dust, unscented options
  • Multiple-cat households — Clumping litter with strong odor control is best
  • Cats with respiratory issues — Dust-free natural or crystal litters
  • Pickyp cats — Start with unscented clumping clay and experiment

Litter Box Maintenance Tips

1. Scoop daily — Remove clumps and solid waste at least once a day

2. Deep clean weekly — Empty, wash with mild soap, and refill with fresh litter

3. Keep it 2-3 inches deep — Most cats prefer this depth

4. One box per cat + one extra — The golden rule for multi-cat homes
